There was no huge stack trace at the end. Just that easy-to-miss pnpm warning: ```text Ignored build scripts: esbuild, sharp Run "pnpm approve-builds" to pick which dependencies should be allowed to run scripts. ``` That warning matters. Since pnpm 10, dependency lifecycle scripts are not treated the same way many people expect from npm. Packages that run `preinstall`, `install`, or `postinstall` can be blocked until you approve them. That is good for supply-chain safety, but it is also exactly how you end up with broken `sharp`, `esbuild`, `@tailwindcss/oxide`, `nx`, `electron`, or `fsevents` installs. Here is the short version: do not fix this by allowing every script in every dependency. Approve the packages that actually need build scripts, commit the config, and make CI use the same decision. ## The Fast Fix Run this first: ```bash pnpm ignored-builds ``` That shows the packages whose build scripts were skipped. Then approve the ones you trust: ```bash pnpm approve-builds ``` pnpm opens an interactive prompt. Pick the native or tooling packages your project really needs. Common examples are: ```text esbuild sharp `@tailwindcss/oxide` nx electron fsevents ``` If you already know the package names, pnpm also supports passing them directly: ```bash pnpm approve-builds esbuild sharp `@tailwindcss/oxide` ``` After that, run install again: ```bash pnpm install ``` Then run the command that was failing before: ```bash pnpm test pnpm build pnpm dev ``` Do not stop at "install passed." The real check is whether the package that needed a compiled binary now works. ## What Changed in pnpm 10 and 11 This is where a lot of old advice gets confusing. In pnpm 10, the older setting was usually `onlyBuiltDependencies` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: ```yaml onlyBuiltDependencies: - esbuild - sharp - `@tailwindcss/oxide` ``` That means only those dependencies are allowed to run lifecycle scripts. Everything else stays blocked. In pnpm 11, the current setting is `allowBuilds`, a map where every package is explicitly allowed or denied: ```yaml allowBuilds: esbuild: true sharp: true "`@tailwindcss/oxide`": true core-js: false ``` That is a cleaner model. You can see the decision in one place: this package may build, that package may not. If your repo is still on pnpm 10, `onlyBuiltDependencies` is normal. If you are on pnpm 11, prefer `allowBuilds`. The official pnpm settings page says the older build settings were replaced by `allowBuilds`, so do not copy a random old snippet without checking your pnpm version. Check it: ```bash pnpm --version ``` ## Fix CI and Docker The interactive prompt is fine on your laptop. It is a bad fit for CI. For CI, the fix is to commit the build approval config. Do not rely on someone clicking the prompt locally and forgetting to commit the result. For pnpm 11, commit something like this: ```yaml # pnpm-workspace.yaml allowBuilds: esbuild: true sharp: true "`@tailwindcss/oxide`": true ``` For pnpm 10, commit this instead: ```yaml # pnpm-workspace.yaml onlyBuiltDependencies: - esbuild - sharp - `@tailwindcss/oxide` ``` Then make the CI install boring: ```bash pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ``` Same idea in Docker: ```dockerfile COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml ./ RUN corepack enable && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ``` The important part is that `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is copied before `pnpm install`. There was no huge stack trace at the end. Just that easy-to-miss pnpm warning: ```text Ignored build scripts: esbuild, sharp Run "pnpm approve-builds" to pick which dependencies should be allowed to run scripts. ``` That warning matters. Since pnpm 10, dependency lifecycle scripts are not treated the same way many people expect from npm. Packages that run `preinstall`, `install`, or `postinstall` can be blocked until you approve them. That is good for supply-chain safety, but it is also exactly how you end up with broken `sharp`, `esbuild`, `@tailwindcss/oxide`, `nx`, `electron`, or `fsevents` installs. Here is the short version: do not fix this by allowing every script in every dependency. Approve the packages that actually need build scripts, commit the config, and make CI use the same decision. ## The Fast Fix Run this first: ```bash pnpm ignored-builds ``` That shows the packages whose build scripts were skipped. Then approve the ones you trust: ```bash pnpm approve-builds ``` pnpm opens an interactive prompt. Pick the native or tooling packages your project really needs. Common examples are: ```text esbuild sharp `@tailwindcss/oxide` nx electron fsevents ``` If you already know the package names, pnpm also supports passing them directly: ```bash pnpm approve-builds esbuild sharp `@tailwindcss/oxide` ``` After that, run install again: ```bash pnpm install ``` Then run the command that was failing before: ```bash pnpm test pnpm build pnpm dev ``` Do not stop at "install passed." The real check is whether the package that needed a compiled binary now works. ## What Changed in pnpm 10 and 11 This is where a lot of old advice gets confusing. In pnpm 10, the older setting was usually `onlyBuiltDependencies` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: ```yaml onlyBuiltDependencies: - esbuild - sharp - `@tailwindcss/oxide` ``` That means only those dependencies are allowed to run lifecycle scripts. Everything else stays blocked. In pnpm 11, the current setting is `allowBuilds`, a map where every package is explicitly allowed or denied: ```yaml allowBuilds: esbuild: true sharp: true "`@tailwindcss/oxide`": true core-js: false ``` That is a cleaner model. You can see the decision in one place: this package may build, that package may not. If your repo is still on pnpm 10, `onlyBuiltDependencies` is normal. If you are on pnpm 11, prefer `allowBuilds`. The official pnpm settings page says the older build settings were replaced by `allowBuilds`, so do not copy a random old snippet without checking your pnpm version. Check it: ```bash pnpm --version ``` ## Fix CI and Docker The interactive prompt is fine on your laptop. It is a bad fit for CI. For CI, the fix is to commit the build approval config. Do not rely on someone clicking the prompt locally and forgetting to commit the result. For pnpm 11, commit something like this: ```yaml # pnpm-workspace.yaml allowBuilds: esbuild: true sharp: true "`@tailwindcss/oxide`": true ``` For pnpm 10, commit this instead: ```yaml # pnpm-workspace.yaml onlyBuiltDependencies: - esbuild - sharp - `@tailwindcss/oxide` ``` Then make the CI install boring: ```bash pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ``` Same idea in Docker: ```dockerfile COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml ./ RUN corepack enable && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ``` The important part is that `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is copied before `pnpm install`. name: Publish tagged package

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "skillplane-v*.*.*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_tag:
        description: "Existing release tag in the form skillplane-v<version>"
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: skillplane-npm-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_tag || github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_tag || github.ref_name }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout release tag
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_tag || github.ref }}

      - name: Verify tagged main revision
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tagged_commit="$(git rev-parse --verify "refs/tags/${RELEASE_TAG}^{commit}")"
          head_commit="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
          if [[ "${tagged_commit}" != "${head_commit}" ]]; then
            echo "HEAD does not match ${RELEASE_TAG}" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "${head_commit}" origin/main; then
            echo "${RELEASE_TAG} must point to a commit on origin/main" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Set up pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 11.9.0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22.13.0
          cache: pnpm
          registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org

      - name: Resolve publish target
        id: resolve
        run: node scripts/resolve-release-tag.mjs "${RELEASE_TAG}"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Verify packed CLI
        run: pnpm cli:release:check

      - name: Publish package
        working-directory: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.pkg_path }}
        run: npm publish --access public --provenance
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

          SKILLPLANE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY }}
          SKILLPLANE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          SKILLPLANE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}

      - name: Deploy app, MCP, and projection Workers
        run: pnpm deploy:all
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_CONTROL_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_DATABASE_URL }}
          AUTHFN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.AUTHFN_SECRET }}
          OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER: ${{ secrets.OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER }}
          TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY: ${{ secrets.TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY }}
          POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN }}
          WORKSPACE_ROUTING_KEYS: ${{ secrets.WORKSPACE_ROUTING_KEYS }}

      - name: Verify app and MCP release
        run: pnpm smoke:production:release

      - name: Deploy docs web app
        run: pnpm deploy:docs
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}

      - name: Preserve encrypted recovery and release evidence
        if: ${{ always() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: production-recovery-${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: |
            .data/production/topology-backups
            .data/production/topology-migration.json
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          include-hidden-files: true
          retention-days: 30

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 180
    environment: production
    env:
      RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_tag || github.ref_name }}
      SKILLPLANE_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_tag || github.ref_name }}
      CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
      CLOUDFLARE_CONTROL_HYPERDRIVE_ID: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_CONTROL_HYPERDRIVE_ID }}
      SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_HYPERDRIVE_ID: ${{ vars.SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_HYPERDRIVE_ID }}
      SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_HYPERDRIVE_ID: ${{ vars.SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_HYPERDRIVE_ID }}
      SKILLPLANE_PUBLIC_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SKILLPLANE_PUBLIC_BUCKET }}
      SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_BUCKET }}
      SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_BUCKET }}
      PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY: ${{ vars.PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout release tag
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_tag || github.ref }}

      - name: Verify tagged main revision
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tagged_commit="$(git rev-parse --verify "refs/tags/${RELEASE_TAG}^{commit}")"
          head_commit="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
          if [[ "${tagged_commit}" != "${head_commit}" ]]; then
            echo "HEAD does not match ${RELEASE_TAG}" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "${head_commit}" origin/main; then
            echo "${RELEASE_TAG} must point to a commit on origin/main" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Set up pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 11.9.0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22.13.0
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Resolve deployment target
        run: node scripts/resolve-cloudflare-tag.mjs "${RELEASE_TAG}"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Validate Cloudflare release
        run: pnpm deploy:check

      - name: Back up and migrate production topology
        run: pnpm db:migrate:topology
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_CONTROL_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY }}
          SKILLPLANE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          SKILLPLANE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}

      - name: Deploy app, MCP, and projection Workers
        run: pnpm deploy:all
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_CONTROL_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_DATABASE_URL }}
          AUTHFN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.AUTHFN_SECRET }}
          OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER: ${{ secrets.OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER }}
          TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY: ${{ secrets.TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY }}
          POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN }}
          WORKSPACE_ROUTING_KEYS: ${{ secrets.WORKSPACE_ROUTING_KEYS }}

      - name: Verify app and MCP release
        run: pnpm smoke:production:release

      - name: Deploy docs web app
        run: pnpm deploy:docs
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}

      - name: Preserve encrypted recovery and release evidence
        if: ${{ always() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: production-recovery-${{ env.RELEASE_TAG }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: |
            .data/production/topology-backups
            .data/production/topology-migration.json
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          include-hidden-files: true
          retention-days: 30

command: sed -n '1,240p' scripts/lib/release-tags.mjs && sed -n '1,180p' scripts/verify-cli-release.mjs && sed -n '1,120p' scripts/resolve-cloudflare-tag.mjs && sed -n '1,240p' scripts/release-tags.test.mjs

# Tagged releases

Skillplane has two independent tag namespaces. Both workflows require the tag
to exist and point to a commit already contained in `origin/main`.

| Tag                            | Result                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `skillplane-v0.1.0`            | Verify, pack, smoke-install, and publish the public `skillplane@0.1.0` package to npm                                                       |
| `skillplane-cloudflare-v0.1.0` | Back up and migrate the production topology, deploy the app/MCP/projection Workers, run production smoke checks, and deploy the docs Worker |

The CLI tag version must exactly match `packages/local-runtime/package.json`.
The Cloudflare version is a release identifier and is recorded as the Wrangler
deployment tag through `SKILLPLANE_RELEASE_TAG`.

## GitHub configuration

Create a protected GitHub environment named `production`. Require deployment
reviewers if production releases need an approval gate. Configure these
environment variables:

- `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`
- `CLOUDFLARE_CONTROL_HYPERDRIVE_ID`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_HYPERDRIVE_ID`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_HYPERDRIVE_ID`
- `SKILLPLANE_PUBLIC_BUCKET`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_BUCKET`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_BUCKET`
- `PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`

Configure these environment secrets:

- `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`
- `SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_DATABASE_URL`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_DATABASE_URL`
- `SKILLPLANE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`
- `SKILLPLANE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`
- `SKILLPLANE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`
- `AUTHFN_SECRET`
- `OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER`
- `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`
- `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`
- `WORKSPACE_ROUTING_KEYS`

The workflow intentionally uses `SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL` as both
the canonical production URL and the control-plane URL, matching the topology
deployment invariant. `WORKSPACE_ROUTING_KEYS` is the complete JSON keyring
required by `deployment/topology.production.json`.

Set the repository secret `NPM_TOKEN` for CLI publication. The workflow also
requests an OIDC token so npm can attach build provenance.

## Creating a release

Update and validate the target version before creating a tag. For example:

```bash
pnpm cli:release:check
git tag skillplane-v0.1.0
git push origin skillplane-v0.1.0
```

For a Cloudflare release, first ensure the tagged commit's migrations and
topology manifest are production-ready:

```bash
pnpm deploy:check
git tag skillplane-cloudflare-v0.1.0
git push origin skillplane-cloudflare-v0.1.0
```

The Cloudflare workflow serializes all production runs and uses the protected
`production` environment. It runs the established blocking sequence:

```text
deploy:check
db:migrate:topology
deploy:all
smoke:production:release
deploy:docs
```

`deploy:all` keeps the existing dependency-safe Worker ordering and performs
its own release smoke before returning. The explicit smoke step remains as the
final app/MCP check before docs deployment. Encrypted topology backups and
migration state are retained as a private workflow artifact for 30 days,
including when a later step fails.

The apex landing Worker at `skillplane.dev` remains excluded because it is
owned and released from the 21n monorepo's `landing/skillplane` workspace.

Both workflows may be rerun manually with `workflow_dispatch`, but the input
must name an existing tag. Manual runs check out the tag itself; they do not
publish or deploy the default branch by accident.
# Production deployment

For the global-control/regional-cell ownership model, routing assertions,
failure behavior, workspace moves, outages, and key rotation, see
[`global-control-plane.md`](./global-control-plane.md). The topology manifest
must be validated and every private cell deployed before enabling gateway mode.

The checked-in transition deployment still deploys the single-cell Skillplane
app and MCP Workers backed by one PostgreSQL database and one private R2 bucket.
The multi-cell renderer in `scripts/lib/topology-deployment.mjs` generates the
next-stage canonical app/MCP gateways plus private app/MCP workers for every
cell in `deployment/topology.production.json`. It requires separate control and
cell Hyperdrive IDs and separate public/regional bucket names. Generated cell
workers have no route, no `workers.dev` exposure, no downstream service
bindings, and no Email Service binding. Promotion of those generated configs is
an explicit rollout step after the cells and projection drainer are provisioned;
it is not an automatic side effect of the legacy `deploy:all` command.

The
landing Worker is maintained and deployed independently from the 21n monorepo's
`landing/skillplane` workspace. The production hosts are
`skillplane.dev`, `app.skillplane.dev`, `mcp.skillplane.dev`, and the PostHog
reverse proxy at `user.skillplane.dev`.

## One-time provider preparation

Before the first release:

1. Create a password-authenticated production PostgreSQL database reachable over
   TLS, enable the provider's managed backup and point-in-time recovery policy,
   and retain its direct URL for migration and backup processes only.
2. Create a Cloudflare Hyperdrive configuration whose origin is that PostgreSQL
   database. Record its 32-character ID. Do not put the direct database URL into
   a Worker variable.
3. Create a production Turnstile widget restricted to
   `app.skillplane.dev`. Record its site key and secret key.
4. Complete Cloudflare Email Service onboarding for `skillplane.dev`, including
   the sender `no-reply@auth.skillplane.dev`, and confirm arbitrary-recipient
   transactional sending is enabled.
5. Create the PostHog managed reverse proxy for `user.skillplane.dev` by
   following the [PostHog reverse-proxy guide](https://posthog.com/docs/advanced/proxy).
   Point an unproxied DNS-only CNAME at the PostHog-provided proxy target and
   wait until PostHog reports the proxy as live.
6. Confirm the Wrangler identity has Workers Scripts, Workers Routes,
   Hyperdrive read, R2 read/write, and Email Sending permissions. The zone must
   be active in the same Cloudflare account.

`pnpm deploy:all` creates `skillplane-skill-bundles` only when it is absent. If
the bucket has no lifecycle action, it adds only a seven-day incomplete
multipart upload abort rule. It then refuses deployment if the bucket has an
object-expiration or storage transition rule, an enabled `r2.dev` URL, or a
custom domain. Published skill bundles never receive age-based deletion.

## Required process inputs

Supply secrets from a password manager or CI secret store. Do not source an
untrusted shell file and do not commit values.

For a controlled local release, place the long-lived values in the ignored
`.env.production.local` file and set its mode to `0600`. Production package
commands ask Node to parse that file without executing it. Existing process
environment variables take precedence. Keep short-lived OTP, Turnstile, and
OAuth verification values in the invoking process when practical, and remove
them immediately after their gate.

Run `pnpm production:secrets:init` once to generate strong independent
`AUTHFN_SECRET`, `OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER`, and
`SKILLPLANE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` values directly into that file. The command
does not print values, rejects duplicate or weak existing assignments, refuses
symlinks, and enforces mode `0600`.

Supply the existing `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` separately; the initializer does
not generate credentials for external services. The renderer exposes that
project token to the browser as `PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` and supplies it to the MCP
Worker as a secret.

| Variable                                              | Purpose                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL`                  | Direct PostgreSQL URL used only by backup, migration, and verification  |
| `SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_MIGRATION_SOURCE_DATABASE_URL` | Temporary old-production URL used only by `db:move:production`          |
| `CLOUDFLARE_HYPERDRIVE_ID`                            | Existing cache-disabled Hyperdrive configuration bound to `HYPERDRIVE`  |
| `SKILLPLANE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`                    | At least 32 characters; encrypts logical backups before they reach disk |
| `AUTHFN_SECRET`                                       | AuthFn signing and tenancy secret, at least 32 characters               |
| `OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER`                                  | OAuth token hashing pepper, at least 32 characters                      |
| `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`                               | Existing PostHog project token used by browser and MCP analytics        |
| `POSTHOG_HOST`                                        | Optional local MCP override; production uses the canonical US host      |
| `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`                                | Production Turnstile secret, at least 32 characters                     |
| `PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`                           | Public site key for the production widget                               |
| `SKILLPLANE_RELEASE_TAG`                              | Optional stable release label; generated when omitted                   |

The one-time multi-cell conversion additionally requires
`SKILLPLANE_CONTROL_DATABASE_URL`, one
`SKILLPLANE_CELL_<REGION>_DATABASE_URL` and
`SKILLPLANE_CELL_<REGION>_BUCKET` per manifest cell, and the public bucket in
`SKILLPLANE_PUBLIC_BUCKET`. `SKILLPLANE_LEGACY_BUCKET` defaults to the legacy
`skillplane-skill-bundles` bucket when omitted. Control and cell database URLs
must all be distinct.
`SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL` must identify the same database as
`SKILLPLANE_CONTROL_DATABASE_URL`; it remains the canonical input to the
encrypted backup workflow. The public and every regional bucket must also be
distinct.

The direct URL may use any PostgreSQL provider, but it must include a host,
username, password, and database name. `sslmode` defaults to `require`; only
`require`, `verify-ca`, and `verify-full` are accepted. The controlled
`insouth.db.21n.dev` alias retains its libpq-compatible TLS behavior. Both backup
and migration query `pg_stat_ssl` and fail if the connection is not encrypted.
Provider URLs using PostgreSQL 17's `sslrootcert=system` hint are normalized for
`node-postgres`, which uses Node's trusted CA set while retaining `verify-full`.
TLS evidence accepts either a certificate-authorized client socket or the
server's `pg_stat_ssl` confirmation, so providers that terminate TLS at a
PostgreSQL proxy remain verifiable without weakening transport security.

`RAILWAY_DATABASE_URL` remains a temporary compatibility alias. New setups must
use `SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL`; if both are present they must resolve
to the same database identity.

The production Hyperdrive configuration must have SQL response caching disabled.
Skillplane is an authorization and mutation control plane, so stale cached reads
can violate permission checks and read-after-write guarantees. Deployment checks
the live configuration and stops before upload if query caching is enabled.

The complete Skillplane source must also be committed with a clean worktree.
The application commit and a digest of all runtime, deployment, package, and
script sources are written to the release manifest. Deployment refuses
untracked or modified source.

## Move production to a new PostgreSQL origin

Keep both raw URLs only for the duration of the move:

```dotenv
REDACTED://new-production...
REDACTED://old-production...
```

Freeze writes to the source, ensure the target is empty, and run with the exact
source and target database names as destructive confirmations:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env node

import { dirname, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { resolvePackageRelease, writeGithubOutputs } from "./lib/release-tags.mjs";

const root = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const release = await resolvePackageRelease(
  process.argv[2] ?? process.env.GITHUB_REF_NAME,
  root,
);

await writeGithubOutputs({
  pkg_slug: release.slug,
  pkg_name: release.name,
  pkg_version: release.version,
  pkg_path: release.path,
});
process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify(release, null, 2)}\n`);

The CLI tag version must exactly match `packages/local-runtime/package.json`.
The Cloudflare version is a release identifier and is recorded as the Wrangler
deployment tag through `SKILLPLANE_RELEASE_TAG`.

## GitHub configuration

Create a protected GitHub environment named `production`. Require deployment
reviewers if production releases need an approval gate. Configure these
environment variables:

- `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`
- `CLOUDFLARE_CONTROL_HYPERDRIVE_ID`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_HYPERDRIVE_ID`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_HYPERDRIVE_ID`
- `SKILLPLANE_PUBLIC_BUCKET`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_BUCKET`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_BUCKET`
- `PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`

Configure these environment secrets:

- `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`
- `SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_DATABASE_URL`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_DATABASE_URL`
- `SKILLPLANE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`
- `SKILLPLANE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`
- `SKILLPLANE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`
- `AUTHFN_SECRET`
- `OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER`
- `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`
- `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`
- `WORKSPACE_ROUTING_KEYS`

The workflow intentionally uses `SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL` as both
the canonical production URL and the control-plane URL, matching the topology
deployment invariant. `WORKSPACE_ROUTING_KEYS` is the complete JSON keyring
required by `deployment/topology.production.json`.

Set the repository secret `NPM_TOKEN` for CLI publication. The workflow also
requests an OIDC token so npm can attach build provenance.

## Creating a release

Update and validate the target version before creating a tag. For example:

```bash
pnpm cli:release:check
git tag skillplane-v0.1.0
git push origin skillplane-v0.1.0
```

For a Cloudflare release, first ensure the tagged commit's migrations and
topology manifest are production-ready:

```bash
pnpm deploy:check
git tag skillplane-cloudflare-v0.1.0
git push origin skillplane-cloudflare-v0.1.0
```

The Cloudflare workflow serializes all production runs and uses the protected
`production` environment. It runs the established blocking sequence:

```text
deploy:check
db:migrate:topology
deploy:all
smoke:production:release
deploy:docs
```

`deploy:all` keeps the existing dependency-safe Worker ordering and performs
its own release smoke before returning. The explicit smoke step remains as the
final app/MCP check before docs deployment. Encrypted topology backups and
migration state are retained as a private workflow artifact for 30 days,
including when a later step fails.

The apex landing Worker at `skillplane.dev` remains excluded because it is
owned and released from the 21n monorepo's `landing/skillplane` workspace.

must name an existing tag. Manual runs check out the tag itself; they do not
publish or deploy the default branch by accident.

For the global-control/regional-cell ownership model, routing assertions,
failure behavior, workspace moves, outages, and key rotation, see
[`global-control-plane.md`](./global-control-plane.md). The topology manifest
must be validated and every private cell deployed before enabling gateway mode.

The checked-in transition deployment still deploys the single-cell Skillplane
app and MCP Workers backed by one PostgreSQL database and one private R2 bucket.
The multi-cell renderer in `scripts/lib/topology-deployment.mjs` generates the
next-stage canonical app/MCP gateways plus private app/MCP workers for every
cell in `deployment/topology.production.json`. It requires separate control and
cell Hyperdrive IDs and separate public/regional bucket names. Generated cell
workers have no route, no `workers.dev` exposure, no downstream service
bindings, and no Email Service binding. Promotion of those generated configs is
an explicit rollout step after the cells and projection drainer are provisioned;
it is not an automatic side effect of the legacy `deploy:all` command.

`landing/skillplane` workspace. The production hosts are
`skillplane.dev`, `app.skillplane.dev`, `mcp.skillplane.dev`, and the PostHog
reverse proxy at `user.skillplane.dev`.

multipart upload abort rule. It then refuses deployment if the bucket has an
object-expiration or storage transition rule, an enabled `r2.dev` URL, or a

untrusted shell file and do not commit values.

| `PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`                           | Public site key for the production widget                               |

# Tagged releases

Skillplane has two independent tag namespaces. Both workflows require the tag
to exist and point to a commit already contained in `origin/main`.

| Tag                            | Result                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `skillplane-v0.1.0`            | Verify, pack, smoke-install, and publish the public `skillplane@0.1.0` package to npm                                                       |
| `skillplane-cloudflare-v0.1.0` | Back up and migrate the production topology, deploy the app/MCP/projection Workers, run production smoke checks, and deploy the docs Worker |

The CLI tag version must exactly match `packages/local-runtime/package.json`.
The Cloudflare version is a release identifier and is recorded as the Wrangler
deployment tag through `SKILLPLANE_RELEASE_TAG`.

## GitHub configuration

Create a protected GitHub environment named `production`. Require deployment
reviewers if production releases need an approval gate. Configure these
environment variables:

- `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`
- `CLOUDFLARE_CONTROL_HYPERDRIVE_ID`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_HYPERDRIVE_ID`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_HYPERDRIVE_ID`
- `SKILLPLANE_PUBLIC_BUCKET`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_BUCKET`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_BUCKET`
- `PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`

Configure these environment secrets:

- `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`
- `SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_DATABASE_URL`
- `SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_DATABASE_URL`
- `SKILLPLANE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`
- `SKILLPLANE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`
- `SKILLPLANE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`
- `AUTHFN_SECRET`
- `OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER`
- `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`
- `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`
- `WORKSPACE_ROUTING_KEYS`

The workflow intentionally uses `SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL` as both
the canonical production URL and the control-plane URL, matching the topology
deployment invariant. `WORKSPACE_ROUTING_KEYS` is the complete JSON keyring
required by `deployment/topology.production.json`.

Set the repository secret `NPM_TOKEN` for CLI publication. The workflow also
requests an OIDC token so npm can attach build provenance.

## Creating a release

Update and validate the target version before creating a tag. For example:

```bash
pnpm cli:release:check
git tag skillplane-v0.1.0
git push origin skillplane-v0.1.0
```

For a Cloudflare release, first ensure the tagged commit's migrations and
topology manifest are production-ready:

```bash
pnpm deploy:check
git tag skillplane-cloudflare-v0.1.0
git push origin skillplane-cloudflare-v0.1.0
```

The Cloudflare workflow serializes all production runs and uses the protected
`production` environment. It runs the established blocking sequence:

```text
deploy:check
db:migrate:topology
deploy:all
smoke:production:release
deploy:docs
```

`deploy:all` keeps the existing dependency-safe Worker ordering and performs
its own release smoke before returning. The explicit smoke step remains as the
final app/MCP check before docs deployment. Encrypted topology backups and
migration state are retained as a private workflow artifact for 30 days,
including when a later step fails.

The apex landing Worker at `skillplane.dev` remains excluded because it is
owned and released from the 21n monorepo's `landing/skillplane` workspace.

Both workflows may be rerun manually with `workflow_dispatch`, but the input
must name an existing tag. Manual runs check out the tag itself; they do not
publish or deploy the default branch by accident.
# Production deployment

For the global-control/regional-cell ownership model, routing assertions,
failure behavior, workspace moves, outages, and key rotation, see
[`global-control-plane.md`](./global-control-plane.md). The topology manifest
must be validated and every private cell deployed before enabling gateway mode.

The checked-in transition deployment still deploys the single-cell Skillplane
app and MCP Workers backed by one PostgreSQL database and one private R2 bucket.
The multi-cell renderer in `scripts/lib/topology-deployment.mjs` generates the
next-stage canonical app/MCP gateways plus private app/MCP workers for every
cell in `deployment/topology.production.json`. It requires separate control and
cell Hyperdrive IDs and separate public/regional bucket names. Generated cell
workers have no route, no `workers.dev` exposure, no downstream service
bindings, and no Email Service binding. Promotion of those generated configs is
an explicit rollout step after the cells and projection drainer are provisioned;
it is not an automatic side effect of the legacy `deploy:all` command.

The
landing Worker is maintained and deployed independently from the 21n monorepo's
`landing/skillplane` workspace. The production hosts are
`skillplane.dev`, `app.skillplane.dev`, `mcp.skillplane.dev`, and the PostHog
reverse proxy at `user.skillplane.dev`.

## One-time provider preparation

Before the first release:

1. Create a password-authenticated production PostgreSQL database reachable over
   TLS, enable the provider's managed backup and point-in-time recovery policy,
   and retain its direct URL for migration and backup processes only.
2. Create a Cloudflare Hyperdrive configuration whose origin is that PostgreSQL
   database. Record its 32-character ID. Do not put the direct database URL into
   a Worker variable.
3. Create a production Turnstile widget restricted to
   `app.skillplane.dev`. Record its site key and secret key.
4. Complete Cloudflare Email Service onboarding for `skillplane.dev`, including
   the sender `no-reply@auth.skillplane.dev`, and confirm arbitrary-recipient
   transactional sending is enabled.
5. Create the PostHog managed reverse proxy for `user.skillplane.dev` by
   following the [PostHog reverse-proxy guide](https://posthog.com/docs/advanced/proxy).
   Point an unproxied DNS-only CNAME at the PostHog-provided proxy target and
   wait until PostHog reports the proxy as live.
6. Confirm the Wrangler identity has Workers Scripts, Workers Routes,
   Hyperdrive read, R2 read/write, and Email Sending permissions. The zone must
   be active in the same Cloudflare account.

`pnpm deploy:all` creates `skillplane-skill-bundles` only when it is absent. If
the bucket has no lifecycle action, it adds only a seven-day incomplete
multipart upload abort rule. It then refuses deployment if the bucket has an
object-expiration or storage transition rule, an enabled `r2.dev` URL, or a
custom domain. Published skill bundles never receive age-based deletion.

## Required process inputs

Supply secrets from a password manager or CI secret store. Do not source an
untrusted shell file and do not commit values.

For a controlled local release, place the long-lived values in the ignored
`.env.production.local` file and set its mode to `0600`. Production package
commands ask Node to parse that file without executing it. Existing process
environment variables take precedence. Keep short-lived OTP, Turnstile, and
OAuth verification values in the invoking process when practical, and remove
them immediately after their gate.

Run `pnpm production:secrets:init` once to generate strong independent
`AUTHFN_SECRET`, `OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER`, and
`SKILLPLANE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` values directly into that file. The command
does not print values, rejects duplicate or weak existing assignments, refuses
symlinks, and enforces mode `0600`.

Supply the existing `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` separately; the initializer does
not generate credentials for external services. The renderer exposes that
project token to the browser as `PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY` and supplies it to the MCP
Worker as a secret.

| Variable                                              | Purpose                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL`                  | Direct PostgreSQL URL used only by backup, migration, and verification  |
| `SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_MIGRATION_SOURCE_DATABASE_URL` | Temporary old-production URL used only by `db:move:production`          |
| `CLOUDFLARE_HYPERDRIVE_ID`                            | Existing cache-disabled Hyperdrive configuration bound to `HYPERDRIVE`  |
| `SKILLPLANE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`                    | At least 32 characters; encrypts logical backups before they reach disk |
| `AUTHFN_SECRET`                                       | AuthFn signing and tenancy secret, at least 32 characters               |
| `OAUTH_TOKEN_PEPPER`                                  | OAuth token hashing pepper, at least 32 characters                      |
| `POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN`                               | Existing PostHog project token used by browser and MCP analytics        |
| `POSTHOG_HOST`                                        | Optional local MCP override; production uses the canonical US host      |
| `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY`                                | Production Turnstile secret, at least 32 characters                     |
| `PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`                           | Public site key for the production widget                               |
| `SKILLPLANE_RELEASE_TAG`                              | Optional stable release label; generated when omitted                   |

The one-time multi-cell conversion additionally requires
`SKILLPLANE_CONTROL_DATABASE_URL`, one
`SKILLPLANE_CELL_<REGION>_DATABASE_URL` and
`SKILLPLANE_CELL_<REGION>_BUCKET` per manifest cell, and the public bucket in
`SKILLPLANE_PUBLIC_BUCKET`. `SKILLPLANE_LEGACY_BUCKET` defaults to the legacy
`skillplane-skill-bundles` bucket when omitted. Control and cell database URLs
must all be distinct.
`SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL` must identify the same database as
`SKILLPLANE_CONTROL_DATABASE_URL`; it remains the canonical input to the
encrypted backup workflow. The public and every regional bucket must also be
distinct.

The direct URL may use any PostgreSQL provider, but it must include a host,
username, password, and database name. `sslmode` defaults to `require`; only
`require`, `verify-ca`, and `verify-full` are accepted. The controlled
`insouth.db.21n.dev` alias retains its libpq-compatible TLS behavior. Both backup
and migration query `pg_stat_ssl` and fail if the connection is not encrypted.
Provider URLs using PostgreSQL 17's `sslrootcert=system` hint are normalized for
`node-postgres`, which uses Node's trusted CA set while retaining `verify-full`.
TLS evidence accepts either a certificate-authorized client socket or the
server's `pg_stat_ssl` confirmation, so providers that terminate TLS at a
PostgreSQL proxy remain verifiable without weakening transport security.

`RAILWAY_DATABASE_URL` remains a temporary compatibility alias. New setups must
use `SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL`; if both are present they must resolve
to the same database identity.

The production Hyperdrive configuration must have SQL response caching disabled.
Skillplane is an authorization and mutation control plane, so stale cached reads
can violate permission checks and read-after-write guarantees. Deployment checks
the live configuration and stops before upload if query caching is enabled.

The complete Skillplane source must also be committed with a clean worktree.
The application commit and a digest of all runtime, deployment, package, and
script sources are written to the release manifest. Deployment refuses
untracked or modified source.

name: Deploy tagged Cloudflare release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "skillplane-cloudflare-v*.*.*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_tag:
        description: "Existing release tag in the form skillplane-cloudflare-v<version>"
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read

jobs:
  queue:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 180
    steps:
      - name: Wait for earlier production releases
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
          CURRENT_RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          CURRENT_RUN_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          workflow="deploy-cloudflare-tag.yml"
          active_statuses=(requested waiting pending queued in_progress)
          while true; do
            blockers=()
            for status in "${active_statuses[@]}"; do
              while IFS= read -r run_id; do
                [[ -n "${run_id}" ]] && blockers+=("${run_id}")
              done < <(
                gh api --paginate --method GET \
                  "repos/${REPOSITORY}/actions/workflows/${workflow}/runs" \
                  -f status="${status}" \
                  -f per_page=100 \
                  --jq ".workflow_runs[] | select(.id != ${CURRENT_RUN_ID}) | select(.run_number < ${CURRENT_RUN_NUMBER}) | .id"
              )
            done
            if [[ "${#blockers[@]}" -eq 0 ]]; then
              break
            fi
            echo "Waiting for ${#blockers[@]} earlier production release run(s): ${blockers[*]}"
            sleep 30
          done

  deploy:
    needs: queue
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 180
    environment: production
    env:
      RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_tag || github.ref_name }}
      SKILLPLANE_RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_tag || github.ref_name }}

      SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_HYPERDRIVE_ID: ${{ vars.SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_HYPERDRIVE_ID }}
      SKILLPLANE_PUBLIC_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SKILLPLANE_PUBLIC_BUCKET }}
      SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_BUCKET }}
      SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_BUCKET }}
      PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY: ${{ vars.PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY }}
    steps:

        uses: pnpm/action-setup@b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 # v4
        with:

      - name: Set up Node.js

        with:
          node-version: 22.13.0

        env:

          SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_CONTROL_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_CELL_IN_SOUTH_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_CELL_US_EAST_DATABASE_URL }}
          SKILLPLANE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY }}

          SKILLPLANE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.SKILLPLANE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}

      - name: Deploy app, MCP, and projection Workers

        env:

name: Publish tagged package

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "skillplane-v*.*.*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_tag:
        description: "Existing release tag in the form skillplane-v<version>"
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: skillplane-npm-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_tag || github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      npm_tag: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.npm_tag }}
    env:
      RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_tag || github.ref_name }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout release tag
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
          ref: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.release_tag || github.sha }}

      - name: Verify tagged main revision
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          tagged_commit="$(git rev-parse --verify "refs/tags/${RELEASE_TAG}^{commit}")"
          head_commit="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
          if [[ "${tagged_commit}" != "${head_commit}" ]]; then
            echo "HEAD does not match ${RELEASE_TAG}" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "${head_commit}" origin/main; then
            echo "${RELEASE_TAG} must point to a commit on origin/main" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Set up pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 # v4
        with:
          version: 11.9.0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
        with:
          node-version: 22.13.0
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Resolve publish target
        id: resolve
        run: node scripts/resolve-release-tag.mjs "${RELEASE_TAG}"

      - name: Install dependencies without lifecycle scripts
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts

      - name: Build reviewed native dependencies
        run: pnpm rebuild esbuild

      - name: Verify packed CLI
        run: pnpm cli:release:check

      - name: Pack verified CLI
        run: pnpm --filter skillplane pack --pack-destination release-artifacts

      - name: Preserve verified package
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        with:
          name: verified-skillplane-package
          path: release-artifacts/*.tgz
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  publish:
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    environment: production
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Set up Node.js for npm
        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
        with:
          node-version: 22.13.0
          registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org

      - name: Restore verified package
        uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          name: verified-skillplane-package
          path: release-artifacts

      - name: Publish package
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mapfile -t archives < <(find release-artifacts -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.tgz')
          if [[ "${#archives[@]}" -ne 1 ]]; then
            echo "Expected exactly one verified package archive" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          npm publish "${archives[0]}" \
            --access public \
            --provenance \
            --tag "${{ needs.verify.outputs.npm_tag }}"
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

PR #22 is updated: [Add tagged npm and Cloudflare release pipelines](https://github.com/21nCo/skillplane/pull/22)

Commit: `04e537772e38a3c1f05ebeb74661925968c14257`

**Fixed**

- Addressed all 15 inline threads, representing 13 deduplicated concerns.
- Pinned release actions to immutable SHAs and disabled checkout credential persistence.
- Checkout now uses the event SHA, detecting moved tags.
- Added durable FIFO Cloudflare release queuing.
- Isolated npm verification from the OIDC-enabled publication job.
- Disabled dependency lifecycle scripts and explicitly rebuilt approved dependencies.
- Routed prereleases to npm `next`; stable releases use `latest`.
- Added strict SemVer and GitHub-output injection validation.
- Fixed fresh-checkout deployment prerequisites, Linux symlink classification, Windows command execution, unused outputs, and Node engine documentation.
- Added a fail-closed production-environment enablement guard.

**Skipped (Already Fixed / Stale)**

- None.

**Not Attempted**

- Repository administration remains required: there is currently no configured `production` environment and only a branch ruleset exists. An administrator must create the protected environment, require reviewers, add both tag rulesets, and set environment variable `PRODUCTION_RELEASES_ENABLED=true`.
- Review threads were not resolved because this round did not authorize GitHub thread mutations.

**Verification**

- `pnpm cli:release:check`: 38 tests, typecheck, build, pack, install, and CLI smoke passed.
- `pnpm deploy:check`: 23 deployment tasks and topology dry-runs passed.
- 6 release regression tests passed.
- Actionlint, YAML parsing, Prettier, targeted ESLint, and diff checks passed.
- npm dry-run confirmed public `skillplane@0.1.0`.
- Local, remote, and PR heads all match `04e5377`.
- Untracked `untitled.md` remains untouched.

One review round is complete. No post-push review refetch, CI polling, or additional loop was performed.

---
name: pr-refetch-fix
description: Run exactly one bounded GitHub PR review-remediation pass: fetch all pending review surfaces, validate findings against the exact PR worktree, fix current valid issues, verify, push one reviewed fix commit to the PR, report, and stop without any post-push refetch, CI wait, or reviewer loop.
---

# PR Refetch Fix

Refetch the current GitHub pull-request review queue, fix the findings that remain valid against the exact PR worktree, verify the affected code, push the fixes to the PR once, report, and stop.

## Absolute single-round boundary

This skill performs exactly one bounded round per invocation.

One round is:

1. identify the PR, authentication context, exact head branch, and dedicated worktree
2. fetch the current review surfaces once
3. classify the fetched findings against the current worktree
4. fix only the valid findings from that fetched snapshot
5. run proportionate local verification
6. when fixes were made, create one reviewed commit and push it to the PR head branch
7. report the result and stop

After step 7, the invocation is complete.

Do not:

- refetch review feedback after the push
- wait for reviewers or bots to analyze the new commit
- poll CI until completion
- begin another fetch/fix/test/push cycle
- keep working because new feedback arrives asynchronously
- interpret "latest", "complete", or "fix pending findings" as permission for an open-ended loop

A second round requires a new, explicit user invocation. If CI or reviewer checks are still running, report them as pending and stop. If no actionable findings are present, report that and stop. If the round is blocked, report the blocker and stop rather than monitoring for a state change.

## Core review rule

Use current unresolved review threads as the primary queue. Timestamp filtering is secondary.

The workflow must prevent these failure modes:

- querying only inline comments after a guessed cutoff
- missing findings in review threads, review bodies, or issue comments
- ignoring an older unresolved thread that is still valid on the current head
- treating every unresolved bot comment as valid without inspecting current code
- fixing against the wrong branch or worktree
- starting an unbounded post-push review loop

## 1. Identify the PR and authentication context

Preserve the user's established GitHub authentication context for every GitHub command, for example:

```bash
GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-other
```

Resolve the repository and PR number from the current branch, worktree, supplied PR URL, or explicit user input.

## 2. Use only the PR's corresponding worktree

Before fetching comments or editing code:

1. locate the PR's dedicated worktree
2. confirm its checked-out branch equals the PR head branch
3. inspect its existing tracked, staged, unstaged, and untracked state
4. preserve unrelated work and artifacts

Minimum checks:

```bash
git branch --show-current
git status --short
git remote -v
```

Treat that exact worktree as the source of truth for code, validation, staging, and commit decisions. Do not validate comments against a main checkout, base branch, sibling branch, or another PR's worktree.

If multiple PRs are requested, each PR is a separate round unless the user explicitly defines one bounded multi-PR round.

## 3. Fetch the current review surfaces once

Start with paginated GraphQL review threads. Fetch every page when more than 100 threads may exist.

```bash
GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-other gh api graphql --paginate -f query='
query($endCursor: String) {
  repository(owner: "OWNER", name: "REPO") {
    pullRequest(number: PR_NUMBER) {
      reviewThreads(first: 100, after: $endCursor) {
        nodes {
          isResolved
          path
          comments(first: 20) {
            nodes {
              body
              author { login }
              createdAt
              outdated
              url
              diffHunk
              originalLine
              line
            }
          }
        }
        pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
      }
    }
  }
}'
```

Then inspect the supplementary surfaces once:

1. PR review bodies
2. PR issue comments
3. raw inline review comments when needed for metadata or export

```bash
GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-other gh pr view PR_NUMBER --repo OWNER/REPO --json headRefOid,reviews,comments,updatedAt,url
```

```bash
GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-other gh api --paginate repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/PR_NUMBER/comments
```

Do not replace unresolved-thread discovery with only `gh pr view --json comments`, only `pulls/<n>/comments`, or only a timestamp query.

## 4. Use timestamps only as a secondary lens

If the user explicitly asks for findings since a push:

1. resolve the exact pushed commit SHA
2. read its absolute UTC timestamp
3. use that timestamp only to describe which feedback arrived later

Still include an older unresolved thread when it remains actionable on the current head.

## 5. Classify before editing

Classify every relevant fetched finding into exactly one status.

### Actionable

- the thread or finding is still pending or unresolved
- it matches the current file and behavior
- the issue is not already fixed
- it is within the authorized scope

### Skipped (Already Fixed / Stale)

- the thread or hunk is outdated
- current code already addresses it
- it describes a prior diff shape
- another current change supersedes it

### Not Attempted

- non-code bot bookkeeping or merge-queue noise
- an unrelated baseline or aggregate quality gate without a concrete scoped finding
- a finding outside the user's authority or requested scope
- a blocked item that cannot be safely changed in this round

Deduplicate multiple reviewers reporting the same root cause so it receives one fix and one status.

## 6. Verify each actionable finding against current code

Before editing:

1. open the current file in the PR worktree
2. inspect the exact code and surrounding contract
3. reproduce or reason through the current behavior
4. check whether existing tests already cover it
5. decide whether the finding is valid now

Do not trust the review diff alone.

## 7. Fix only valid findings from the fetched snapshot

Make the narrowest complete fixes tied to the actionable findings. Add focused regression coverage when practical.

Preserve unrelated dirty work. Keep unrelated untracked and `.conduct/` artifacts out of commits unless explicitly requested.

Do not expand into repository-wide cleanup merely because a bot reports an aggregate quality gate.

## 8. Verify locally

Run focused tests first, then the relevant typecheck, lint, test, and build gates in proportion to risk. Distinguish:

- failures caused by the changes
- pre-existing or unrelated failures
- local proof
- pending external CI or reviewer state

Do not wait for external CI as part of this skill. A single immediate check snapshot is allowed only for reporting; no polling.

## 9. Commit and push the fixes exactly once

Invoking this skill authorizes one reviewed commit and one normal push of the fixes produced by this round to the PR head branch. Do not leave completed fixes only in the local worktree. If the fetched snapshot contains no actionable findings and no changes were made, do not create an empty commit or push.

Before committing:

1. review the exact staged allowlist
2. run `git diff --cached --check`
3. confirm unrelated artifacts are excluded

Create exactly one commit for the reviewed fix batch and push it once to the PR head branch. Do not force-push. Verify the local, remote, and PR head SHAs once after pushing.

Do not refetch review feedback after the push. Do not wait for the pushed commit to receive new reviews.

## 10. Report and terminate

Report with these explicit buckets:

- `Fixed`
- `Skipped (Already Fixed / Stale)`
- `Not Attempted`
- `Verification`

Include the exact pushed commit SHA and PR URL. If no changes were needed, say explicitly that no commit or push was created. State any pending CI or reviewer checks without waiting for them.

End with a clear termination statement such as:

> One review round is complete. No post-push refetch or additional review loop was performed.

Then stop.

name: pr-refetch-fix
description: Run exactly one bounded GitHub PR review-remediation pass: fetch all pending review surfaces, validate findings against the exact PR worktree, fix current valid issues, verify, push one reviewed fix commit to the PR, report, and stop without any post-push refetch, CI wait, or reviewer loop.
---

# PR Refetch Fix

Refetch the current GitHub pull-request review queue, fix the findings that remain valid against the exact PR worktree, verify the affected code, push the fixes to the PR once, report, and stop.

## Absolute single-round boundary

This skill performs exactly one bounded round per invocation.

One round is:

1. identify the PR, authentication context, exact head branch, and dedicated worktree
2. fetch the current review surfaces once
3. classify the fetched findings against the current worktree
4. fix only the valid findings from that fetched snapshot
5. run proportionate local verification
6. when fixes were made, create one reviewed commit and push it to the PR head branch
7. report the result and stop

After step 7, the invocation is complete.

Do not:

- refetch review feedback after the push
- wait for reviewers or bots to analyze the new commit
- poll CI until completion
- begin another fetch/fix/test/push cycle
- keep working because new feedback arrives asynchronously
- interpret "latest", "complete", or "fix pending findings" as permission for an open-ended loop

A second round requires a new, explicit user invocation. If CI or reviewer checks are still running, report them as pending and stop. If no actionable findings are present, report that and stop. If the round is blocked, report the blocker and stop rather than monitoring for a state change.

## Core review rule

Use current unresolved review threads as the primary queue. Timestamp filtering is secondary.

The workflow must prevent these failure modes:

- querying only inline comments after a guessed cutoff
- missing findings in review threads, review bodies, or issue comments
- ignoring an older unresolved thread that is still valid on the current head
- treating every unresolved bot comment as valid without inspecting current code
- fixing against the wrong branch or worktree
- starting an unbounded post-push review loop

## 1. Identify the PR and authentication context

Preserve the user's established GitHub authentication context for every GitHub command, for example:

```bash
GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-other
```

Resolve the repository and PR number from the current branch, worktree, supplied PR URL, or explicit user input.

## 2. Use only the PR's corresponding worktree

Before fetching comments or editing code:

1. locate the PR's dedicated worktree
2. confirm its checked-out branch equals the PR head branch
3. inspect its existing tracked, staged, unstaged, and untracked state
4. preserve unrelated work and artifacts

Minimum checks:

```bash
git branch --show-current
git status --short
git remote -v
```

Treat that exact worktree as the source of truth for code, validation, staging, and commit decisions. Do not validate comments against a main checkout, base branch, sibling branch, or another PR's worktree.

If multiple PRs are requested, each PR is a separate round unless the user explicitly defines one bounded multi-PR round.

## 3. Fetch the current review surfaces once

Start with paginated GraphQL review threads. Fetch every page when more than 100 threads may exist.

```bash
GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-other gh api graphql --paginate -f query='
query($endCursor: String) {
  repository(owner: "OWNER", name: "REPO") {
    pullRequest(number: PR_NUMBER) {
      reviewThreads(first: 100, after: $endCursor) {
        nodes {
          isResolved
          path
          comments(first: 20) {
            nodes {
              body
              author { login }
              createdAt
              outdated
              url
              diffHunk
              originalLine
              line
            }
          }
        }
        pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
      }
    }
  }
}'
```

Then inspect the supplementary surfaces once:

1. PR review bodies
2. PR issue comments
3. raw inline review comments when needed for metadata or export

```bash
GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-other gh pr view PR_NUMBER --repo OWNER/REPO --json headRefOid,reviews,comments,updatedAt,url
```

```bash
GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-other gh api --paginate repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/PR_NUMBER/comments
```

Do not replace unresolved-thread discovery with only `gh pr view --json comments`, only `pulls/<n>/comments`, or only a timestamp query.

## 4. Use timestamps only as a secondary lens

If the user explicitly asks for findings since a push:

1. resolve the exact pushed commit SHA
2. read its absolute UTC timestamp
3. use that timestamp only to describe which feedback arrived later

Still include an older unresolved thread when it remains actionable on the current head.

## 5. Classify before editing

Classify every relevant fetched finding into exactly one status.

### Actionable

- the thread or finding is still pending or unresolved
- it matches the current file and behavior
- the issue is not already fixed
- it is within the authorized scope

### Skipped (Already Fixed / Stale)

- the thread or hunk is outdated
- current code already addresses it
- it describes a prior diff shape
- another current change supersedes it

### Not Attempted

- non-code bot bookkeeping or merge-queue noise
- an unrelated baseline or aggregate quality gate without a concrete scoped finding
- a finding outside the user's authority or requested scope
- a blocked item that cannot be safely changed in this round

Deduplicate multiple reviewers reporting the same root cause so it receives one fix and one status.

## 6. Verify each actionable finding against current code

Before editing:

1. open the current file in the PR worktree
2. inspect the exact code and surrounding contract
3. reproduce or reason through the current behavior
4. check whether existing tests already cover it
5. decide whether the finding is valid now

Do not trust the review diff alone.

## 7. Fix only valid findings from the fetched snapshot

Make the narrowest complete fixes tied to the actionable findings. Add focused regression coverage when practical.

Preserve unrelated dirty work. Keep unrelated untracked and `.conduct/` artifacts out of commits unless explicitly requested.

Do not expand into repository-wide cleanup merely because a bot reports an aggregate quality gate.

## 8. Verify locally

Run focused tests first, then the relevant typecheck, lint, test, and build gates in proportion to risk. Distinguish:

- failures caused by the changes
- pre-existing or unrelated failures
- local proof
- pending external CI or reviewer state

Do not wait for external CI as part of this skill. A single immediate check snapshot is allowed only for reporting; no polling.

## 9. Commit and push the fixes exactly once

Invoking this skill authorizes one reviewed commit and one normal push of the fixes produced by this round to the PR head branch. Do not leave completed fixes only in the local worktree. If the fetched snapshot contains no actionable findings and no changes were made, do not create an empty commit or push.

Before committing:

1. review the exact staged allowlist
2. run `git diff --cached --check`
3. confirm unrelated artifacts are excluded

Create exactly one commit for the reviewed fix batch and push it once to the PR head branch. Do not force-push. Verify the local, remote, and PR head SHAs once after pushing.

Do not refetch review feedback after the push. Do not wait for the pushed commit to receive new reviews.

## 10. Report and terminate

Report with these explicit buckets:

- `Fixed`
- `Skipped (Already Fixed / Stale)`
- `Not Attempted`
- `Verification`

Include the exact pushed commit SHA and PR URL. If no changes were needed, say explicitly that no commit or push was created. State any pending CI or reviewer checks without waiting for them.

End with a clear termination statement such as:

> One review round is complete. No post-push refetch or additional review loop was performed.

Then stop.

name: composio-cli
description: Help users operate the published Composio CLI to find the right tool, connect accounts, inspect schemas, execute tools, subscribe to trigger events with `composio listen`, script workflows with `composio run`, and call authenticated app APIs with `composio proxy`. Use when the user asks how to do something with `composio`, wants to run a known tool slug, needs to discover a slug with `composio search`, fix a missing connection with `composio link`, inspect tool inputs with `--get-schema` or `--dry-run`, troubleshoot top-level CLI flows, or explicitly needs `composio dev` guidance.
---

<!-- AUTO-GENERATED: edit skills-src/composio-cli/index.ts and rebuild -->
<!-- release-channel: stable -->

# Composio CLI

## Default Workflow

1. Start with `composio execute <slug>` whenever the slug is known.
2. If several independent tool calls must happen at once, use `composio execute -p/--parallel` with repeated `<slug> -d <json>` groups.
3. If `execute` says the toolkit is not connected, run `composio link <toolkit>` and retry.
4. If the arguments are unclear, run `composio execute <slug> --get-schema` or `--dry-run` before guessing.
5. Reach for `composio search "<task>"` only when the slug is unknown. `search` accepts one or more queries, so batch related discovery work into a single command when useful.

## `execute` - Run A Tool

Use `execute` when the tool slug is already known.

```bash
composio execute GITHUB_GET_THE_AUTHENTICATED_USER -d '{}'
```

Inspect required inputs without executing:
```bash
composio execute GITHUB_CREATE_AN_ISSUE --get-schema
```

Preview safely:
```bash
composio execute GITHUB_CREATE_AN_ISSUE --skip-connection-check --dry-run -d '{ owner: "acme", repo: "app", title: "Bug report", body: "Steps to reproduce..." }'
```

Pass data from a file or stdin:
```bash
composio execute GITHUB_CREATE_AN_ISSUE -d @issue.json
cat issue.json | composio execute GITHUB_CREATE_AN_ISSUE -d -
```

Upload a local file:
```bash
composio execute SLACK_UPLOAD_OR_CREATE_A_FILE_IN_SLACK \
  --file ./image.png \
  -d '{ channels: "C123" }'
```

Run independent tool calls in parallel:
```bash
composio execute --parallel \
  GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL -d '{ recipient_email: "a@b.com", subject: "Hi" }' \
  GITHUB_CREATE_AN_ISSUE -d '{ owner: "acme", repo: "app", title: "Bug" }'
```

Key flags:
- `--get-schema`: Inspect required arguments without executing the tool.
- `--dry-run`: Preview the request shape without performing the action.
- `--file`: Inject a local file path into a tool that exposes exactly one uploadable file argument.
- `--parallel`: Execute multiple independent tool calls in the same invocation.
- `--account`: Select which connected account to use by alias, word_id, or account id when multiple accounts exist for the same toolkit.

- `--file` only works when the tool exposes a single uploadable file input. Otherwise use explicit `-d` JSON.

## `search` - Find The Slug

Use `search` only when the tool slug is not already known.

```bash
composio search "create a github issue"
composio search "send an email" --toolkits gmail
composio search "send an email" "create a github issue"
composio search "my emails" "my github issues" --toolkits gmail,github
```

- Batch related discovery work into one `search` invocation, then move back to `execute` once the correct slugs are known.

## `link` - Connect An Account

Use `link` when `execute` reports that a toolkit is not connected, or when the user explicitly wants to authorize an account.

```bash
composio link gmail
composio link googlecalendar --no-browser
```

Key flags:
- `--alias`: Assign an alias to the connected account. Required when creating an additional account for the same toolkit.

- Retry the original `execute` command after linking succeeds.

## `proxy` - Raw API Access

Use `proxy` when a toolkit supports a raw API operation that is easier than finding a dedicated tool slug.

```bash
composio proxy https://api.github.com/user --toolkit github --account work --method GET </dev/null
```

Key flags:
- `--account`: Select which connected account to use by alias, word_id, or account id.

## `run` - Scripting, LLMs, and Programmatic Workflows

For programmatic calls, loops, output plumbing, or anything beyond a single tool call, prefer `composio run`.

`composio run` executes an inline ESM JavaScript/TypeScript snippet with authenticated `execute()`, `search()`, `proxy()`, and the experimental `experimental_subAgent()` helper pre-injected. No SDK setup required.

Chain multiple tools:
```bash
composio run '
  const me = await execute("GITHUB_GET_THE_AUTHENTICATED_USER");
  const emails = await execute("GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", { max_results: 1 });
  console.log({ login: me.data.login, fetchedEmails: !!emails.data });
'
```

Fan out with Promise.all:
```bash
composio run '
  const [me, emails] = await Promise.all([
    execute("GITHUB_GET_THE_AUTHENTICATED_USER"),
    execute("GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", { max_results: 5 }),
  ]);
  console.log({ login: me.data.login, emailCount: emails.data.messages?.length });
'
```

Feed tool output into an LLM and get structured JSON back:
```bash
composio run --logs-off '
  const emails = await execute("GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", { max_results: 5 });
  const brief = await experimental_subAgent(
    `Summarize these emails and count them.\n\n${emails.prompt()}`,
    { schema: z.object({ summary: z.string(), count: z.number() }) }
  );
  console.log(brief.structuredOutput);
'
```

- Use top-level `execute --parallel` instead when the user only needs a few independent tool calls and does not need script logic.

## Auth

```bash
composio whoami   # check current session
composio login    # authenticate if whoami fails
```

## Escalate Only When Needed

If the user is stuck on top-level commands or needs fallback inspection commands, load [references/troubleshooting.md](references/troubleshooting.md).

If the user explicitly asks about developer projects, auth configs, connected accounts, triggers, logs, orgs, or projects, load [references/composio-dev.md](references/composio-dev.md). `composio dev` is not the default end-user path.
